tldr:
For the difference of whole-population marginal standardized causal skewnesses \(\theta=\kappa_1-\kappa_0\), the stipulated rare ternary H\"older-\(1/8\) class has the sharp finite-sample absolute-risk and \(0.90\)-honest connected-interval length profile
\[
g(n,q)=h(n,q)=\min\{1,(nq^2)^{-1/2}+(nq)^{-1/3}\}.
\]
Universal constants hold for every public \(n\ge2\) and \(q\in(0,1/16]\). Total procedures using only original records attain this profile, and original-likelihood comparisons within the same class match it. The three regimes are saturation below \(q=n^{-1/2}\), signed-information precision up to \(q=n^{-1/4}\), and rough-confounding precision above that elbow, with empty regimes omitted. Uniform consistent estimation and shrinking honest intervals are possible exactly when \(nq_n^2\to\infty\). The unknown variance denominator is estimated and controlled uniformly.

Separate application of the carried endpoint certificates gives \(b_{\mathrm{sep}}\), and both optimal scalar decision values are \(o(b_{\mathrm{sep}})\), along sequences for which that certificate vanishes, exactly when \(q_n\to0\). The signed and unsigned marks preserve the smaller joint-class cancellation. The endpoint pair is measurably equivalent to the original ternary outcome, so this separation concerns a certificate calculation, not a restriction on the information available to endpoint-based procedures. The smooth skewness map and higher-order correction architecture are credited infrastructure.
